primary_source.author: Claude Sabbah
primary_source.title: Hypergeometric periods for a tame polynomial
primary_source.actual_reading: Introduction Fourier-Laplace description; Section1 definitions and equations(1.1),(1.2), Lemma1.3 (printed pages5-6); full Section12, Theorem12.1, Lemma12.2 and its proof (printed pages32-33). Not a full-manuscript read.
primary_source.imported_result: Affine convenient Newton-nondegenerate polynomial: regular-singular Fourier-Laplace module at tau=0 and N_alpha G=V_alpha G. Polynomial volume of Newton degree1 lies in V_1. Increasing convention: tau*partial_tau+alpha nilpotent on gr_alpha^V.
primary_source.use_boundary: Actual filtration membership is used, not only equality of spectral multisets. This is the affine-polynomial theorem, not a Laurent-torus theorem. The regular-singular decomposition gives all horizontal evaluations on V_1 growth at most |tau|^-1 times a finite logarithm power.

new_internal_argument: Nodal form Tuv+a*u^3+d*v^3, a*d!=0, with arbitrary nondegenerate transformed Gaussian metric. Nonisotropic node supplies T^2 intercept. All13 outer faces are nondegenerate; all three positive facet weights sum to1. Rescaling x=z/t identifies the original connection seed with t^-3*omega in the pullback lambda=t^-2 of the fixed exponential module. A constant pure-moment series extends from its seed submodule to a horizontal functional and forces omega evaluation lambda^-3/2, contradicting V_1 growth. No rapid-decay comparison is required for this extension.

CUSPIDAL_CUBIC_SHARP_THRESHOLD.md and REDUCIBLE_CUBIC_CLASSIFICATION.md: complete respective homogeneous classes, sharp gates and mixed cutoff.

source_reconciliation: The recent November stationary-phase and correlated-replica sources were already audited in the linked earlier source records. This new route uses an older precise affine Newton theorem; no claim of a new latest-version bibliographic sweep or exhaustive novelty search.
rejected_shortcuts: Equality of spectra alone does not establish the needed volume-form membership.
Real or generic-Morse stationary phase does not bound all complex horizontal functionals.
Leaving the mixed binary cubic terms before the Newton-face check can introduce degeneracy.
Ignoring the t^-3 volume factor changes the decisive exponent.
Nonhomogeneous perturbations do not give the same fixed f after rescaling.
A Gaussian quadratic saturates exponent3/2; the strict Newton gap is essential.
